prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: one high-fidelity desktop website homepage direction comp for fcullmann.com, presented as the complete first viewport only
Primary request: Design a shippable desktop web UI direction called “Focused Utility Hub” for Florian Ullmann’s personal developer-tools website. It must feel like a confident, modern utility product with a distinct personal signature, not an anonymous tools directory and not a generic marketing landing page.
Input images: Image 1 is a structural and style reference only. Borrow only the idea of a light cool utility platform, compact navigation, filterable catalogue, and crisp card density. Do not copy its branding, logo, exact layout, content, proportions, colors, icons, or wording.
Canvas: exact visual composition for a 1504 × 1046 pixel landscape desktop viewport, edge-to-edge website screenshot with no browser chrome, no device frame.
Style/medium: realistic high-fidelity product UI, clean application chrome, precise responsive grid, confident workhorse sans-serif, crisp readable typography, polished enough for a design decision board. More product energy and personal authorship than the reference while remaining in the same modern utility-site family.
Color palette: main background #F7F8FC; white surfaces; near-black #20232B text; indigo #4F46E5 primary; teal #14A38B and coral #F06348 as restrained category accents. Use subtle tinted category fields, soft cool-gray borders, 12–16px corner radii, shallow elevation, excellent contrast.
Composition and hierarchy:
1. Restrained 64px header. Left: simple original text wordmark “fcullmann.com” with a tiny abstract code-bracket accent, not a copied logo. Center navigation: “Tools”, “Projects”, “Writing”, “About”. Right: compact language control showing “EN” active and “DE”, plus a small outlined “All tools” button. No sign-in, registration, metrics, social icons, or unrelated controls.
2. A medium-height split introduction, approximately 270px, not a huge generic hero. Left side is wider and left-aligned. Small eyebrow exactly “FLORIAN ULLMANN · SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER”. Headline exactly “Useful tools. Clear thinking.” Supporting copy exactly “Browser-based developer tools, projects, and technical writing — built and maintained by Florian Ullmann.” Primary button “Explore tools”; secondary text link “Latest writing”. Add one restrained personal detail line: “Practical software for everyday technical work.”
3. Right side of the introduction is a compact white discovery panel titled “Find a tool”. Include a wide search input with placeholder “Search 50+ tools” to communicate catalogue scalability without claiming actual tool count; category pills “All”, “Format”, “Encode”, “Generate”, “Documents”; and a featured shortcut row “Quick open  JSON Formatter  →”. Make the panel feel functional, not decorative.
4. Directly below, a dense section header “Featured tools” with compact supporting label “Everyday browser utilities” and a right link “View all tools”. Then exactly five equal-width tool cards in one row, designed as a repeatable scalable catalogue system. Each card uses a small original geometric line icon, a tinted category field, title, one concise description, a small category label, and an “Open tool →” action. Card content:
- “JSON Formatter” — “Format and validate JSON in your browser.” — category “FORMAT” — indigo accent.
- “Base64 Encoder” — “Encode and decode text locally.” — category “ENCODE” — teal accent.
- “UUID Generator” — “Generate UUIDs in one click.” — category “GENERATE” — coral accent.
- “URL Encoder” — “Encode and decode URLs safely.” — category “ENCODE” — indigo accent.
- “PDF Converter” — visible status badge “PLANNED”; description “Document conversion tools are on the roadmap.” — category “DOCUMENTS” — muted cool gray; action text “Planned”, not “Open tool”.
5. At the lower fold, still clearly visible, show a compact category navigation strip titled “Browse by category” with four clean tiles or tabs: “Data & JSON”, “Encoding”, “Generators”, “Documents”. Beside or directly below it, show a “Latest Writing” area with the honest empty-state line “Technical notes are coming soon.” and a link “View writing”. The viewport should end naturally while both headings and their first-row content remain visible.
Layout details: centered 1400px content frame with approximately 40–48px outer margins; compact but generous vertical rhythm; precise 12-column logic; dense five-column shelf; clean alignment; shallow shadows; subtle one-pixel borders; small restrained abstract code marks or dotted grid texture only if needed for personal signature. Preserve ample whitespace without sacrificing catalogue density.
Text rendering: Render every quoted string verbatim, correctly spelled, fully legible, and only once in its specified area. English UI only except the “DE” locale label. Use typographic hierarchy and avoid tiny unreadable body copy.
Constraints: use only these confirmed facts: Florian Ullmann; Senior Software Engineer; browser developer tools, projects, technical writing; JSON Formatter; Base64 Encoder; UUID Generator; URL Encoder; PDF Converter is Planned. Do not invent usage metrics, clients, testimonials, biographies, portrait, project claims, article titles, dates, social links, or product capabilities. No browser chrome, no device frame, no watermark.
Avoid: Bootstrap appearance; copied reference branding or layout; atlas, map, compass, globe, paper, notebook, scrapbook, serif identity; dark theme; giant gradient hero; oversized marketing headline; stock photography; portraits; 3D illustrations; fake dashboards; fake charts; excessive glassmorphism; busy decoration; rounded-everything toy aesthetic; malformed text.
